items.description: Mount Cameroon is a steep volcanic massif on the coast of southwestern Cameroon. It rises sharply above the Atlantic lowlands.
The Mandara Mountains run along Cameroon's far northern border. They form a rugged upland landscape with narrow valleys and rocky ridges.
The Bamenda Highlands are a cool, elevated region in northwest Cameroon. Their plateau terrain shapes settlement and farming.
The Sanaga basin covers a vast central drainage area. It is one of the main structural landscapes of Cameroon.
Mount Manengouba is a volcanic mountain with crater lakes in western Cameroon. Its high slopes stand above the surrounding countryside.
Mount Kupe is a steep forested peak in southwestern Cameroon. It rises above the coastal plain and supports dense mountain vegetation.
Mount Oissa is part of the highland relief in western Cameroon. It belongs to the hill country that breaks up the plateau surface.
The Nlonako Mountains form a rugged range in western Cameroon. They add steep relief and forest cover to the area.
Mount Bambouto is a volcanic highland in western Cameroon. It forms part of the country's well known grassland mountain belt.
Mount Tchabal Mbabo rises in the Adamawa region as a high volcanic massif. It is one of the area's prominent upland forms.
Mount Oku is a high mountain in northwest Cameroon. It belongs to the volcanic chain that shapes the Bamenda highlands.
The Rumpi Hills are a rugged mountain group in the southwest. Their steep slopes and wet forests create a distinct relief zone.
The Bakossi Mountains form a forested highland in western Cameroon. They are known for steep slopes and a wet mountain climate.
Mount Koupe is a steep forest mountain in southwestern Cameroon. It overlooks the coastal lowlands with a sharp rise in elevation.
The Ntem area includes elevated terrain in the south of Cameroon. Its relief is shaped by forested hills and river valleys.
